title: Asset extraction: graphics and music out of ROMs

units.title: Literature review: GBA asset formats and rippers
units.detail: Asset extraction (docs/decisions.md, decision 2, 'Two views of a ROM', june 2026-10-26): graphics and music out of a ROM with no hand reading of its code, by watching where the game's data goes at run time. Emerald first; pret's pokeemerald (graphics as PNG, music as MIDI) is the oracle. A review of primary sources and tool source (not summaries), each added to docs/references.md: the GBA's tile, palette, OAM and BG map formats; BIOS compression (LZ77, RL, Huffman, Diff); Nintendo's m4a/Sappy sound engine (song table, voicegroups, samples) and the tools that parse it (agbplay, gba-mus-ripper, sappy2midi); pret's own extraction tools (gbagfx, mid2agb, wav2agb) and the layout of pokeemerald's graphics/ and sound/; mGBA's tile and sprite viewers; Aseprite's file format and Rust crates for writing it; any prior work on finding assets dynamically (provenance or taint tracking in emulators). Write docs/research/asset-extraction.md.

record.evidence: docs/research/asset-extraction.md (commit fc2aaa2): GBA tile/palette/OAM/map formats, BIOS LZ77/RL/Huffman/Diff vs our HLE, pokeemerald graphics/ and sound/ measured (3,850 PNG, 530 MIDI, 610-entry song table), gbagfx/mid2agb/wav2agb, m4a structs and run-time discovery via 0x03007FF0, agbplay/gba-mus-ripper/saptapper/VGMusicStudio, mGBA viewers, CDLs, taint costs, texture-replacement keying, Aseprite spec and crates. Sources with commits in references.md; just check passes after merging main.

units.title: Spike: tag VRAM, palette and OAM bytes with their source
units.detail: Asset extraction (docs/decisions.md, decision 2, 'Two views of a ROM', june 2026-10-26): graphics and music out of a ROM with no hand reading of its code, by watching where the game's data goes at run time. Emerald first; pret's pokeemerald (graphics as PNG, music as MIDI) is the oracle. In the interpreter (or the runtime, if cheaper), record for every byte written to VRAM, palette RAM, OAM and the sound FIFOs where it came from: a ROM address and the transform (CPU copy, CpuSet/CpuFastSet, DMA, BIOS decompression, or computed). Run the Emerald new-game route and report: how much of VRAM and palette RAM traces back to a ROM address, through which transforms, how many distinct source blobs, and what stays unexplained (drawn by the CPU, built from tables). Costs: time per frame with tagging on; off by default, so the normal run is unchanged.

record.evidence: just provenance emerald-newgame (runtime::prov behind a feature; docs/research/assets-provenance.md): at the truck VRAM's non-zero bytes are 90.3% from ROM (62% LZ77+DMA, 15% CPU copy+DMA, 11% DMA, 3% CpuSet), 9.7% computed text tiles; menus 74-94% computed (font renderer). Palette is computed by the fade everywhere, but 90-100% equals ROM-copied gPlttBufferUnfaded (0x02037714, found by the report). OAM 46% ROM templates, rest computed; FIFOs 100% computed (mixer). Blobs: 37 LZ77, all at pret gfx symbols; 58 copied ranges, 57 in data symbols. Cost ~5%/frame (3.75-3.96 vs 3.91-4.26 ms); same truck hash 26c2f9d4009c5696. just check passes after merging main.

units.title: Asset overrides: the runtime serves edited assets
units.detail: Asset extraction (docs/decisions.md, decision 2, 'Two views of a ROM', june 2026-10-26): graphics and music out of a ROM with no hand reading of its code, by watching where the game's data goes at run time. Emerald first; pret's pokeemerald is the oracle. Design: docs/asset-extraction-design.md. The design's Overrides section: a mod's mod.toml [assets] maps a manifest ROM address to an edited PNG, .aseprite or .pal; crates/assets encodes it back to the blob's unpacked bytes; the runtime gets a sorted static table: HLE LZ77 and RL write the override instead of decoding (size must equal the header's), raw blobs come from a patched ROM copy whose CRC stays the original's. Off without a mod folder, so play-view hashes are unchanged. Refuse an override of a range codegen's const-prop folds loads from, in a recompiled build. Check: an edited sprite (Aseprite) and tile sheet (PNG) show in game in both builds; an unedited export round-trips to identical frames.

record.evidence: Review fix made: the folded-range refusal in crates/desktop/src/lib.rs now continues its literal with a trailing backslash, so it reads '…{e:#010x}, which this recompiled build's code…'; the test asset_overrides_patch_a_copy_and_refuse_folded_bytes now asserts that text. Earlier evidence stands (edited Aseprite sprite and PNG tile sheet in both builds, unedited round-trip identical). just check passes after merging origin/main (6f624c6).

units.title: Load and use logs for asset export
units.detail: Asset extraction (docs/decisions.md, decision 2, 'Two views of a ROM', june 2026-10-26): graphics and music out of a ROM with no hand reading of its code, by watching where the game's data goes at run time. Emerald first; pret's pokeemerald is the oracle. Design: docs/asset-extraction-design.md. The design's Recording section: the load log (every BIOS decompression, DMA, CpuSet, CpuFastSet whose source traces to ROM, with its full length: bytes the decoder read, or the copy's count) and the use log (per VBlank, changes only: BG and OBJ tiles shown, their blob and offset, palette bank and its palette blob via the unfaded-buffer value match), from `just assets-record ROUTE` into out/assets/<game>/<route>/. Check: on Emerald's new-game route every one of the provenance spike's 37 compressed blobs and 58 copied ranges is in the load log with its full length, and every BG and OBJ tile shown at the truck has a use record.

record.evidence: just assets-record emerald-newgame (after merging main): out/assets/emerald/emerald-newgame/check.txt PASS. 37 of 37 compressed blobs decompressed in loads.tsv, each length equal to pret's symbol size; 58 of 58 copied ranges, every byte in a load; 2,624 of 2,624 tiles shown at the truck (frame 5400) have a use record, 1,973 from a loaded blob, 651 the computed text window, all banks' palettes found. just check passes. Unit test for gbaa-assets check-load-log. No subagent review (the loop reviews the diff).

units.title: Sprites from OAM with animations to Aseprite
units.detail: Asset extraction (docs/decisions.md, decision 2, 'Two views of a ROM', june 2026-10-26): graphics and music out of a ROM with no hand reading of its code, by watching where the game's data goes at run time. Emerald first; pret's pokeemerald is the oracle. Design: docs/asset-extraction-design.md. The design's Sprites and animations section: assemble sprites from OAM (1D and 2D mapping), frames of one sheet laid out as pret's -mwidth/-mheight strips, animation sequences and timing per OAM index as Aseprite frames, durations and tags, composed multi-entry sprites, user data with ROM address and palette. aseprite-io 0.2.0, every file round-tripped through it and asefile; own writer if that fails. Check: pret's object-event and Pokémon strips the route shows match at the image level; report animations found.

record.evidence: just assets-check-sprites: object-event and Pokémon strips at image level 3 of 3 (Brendan walking 9 frames across, moving box, Lotad 2 down; sheet PNG and every Aseprite sheet frame vs pret's PNG), other sheets 7 of 12; 15 sheets, 7 animations found (Brendan's walk-in-place loop 3,0,4,0 x8 frames = pret sAnim_GoSouth). Every .aseprite round-tripped through aseprite-io and asefile. Graphics check bytes 79->81, image 11->20 of 57; just check passes.

notes.text: From graphics-export: raw copies merge only on overlap, so a strip DMA'd a frame at a time (Brendan walking 0x084975f8, 0x084978f8...) arrives as one tile blob per frame; join them by pret symbol range. Image level fails mostly on layout width, yours to fix.

uses.tsv from {unit:assets/load-log} is aggregated (one line per distinct use, first/last frame, frames shown): no per-frame OAM sequence. Animation timing needs a per-frame OBJ record added to crates/desktop/src/assets_log.rs.

units.title: Emerald's samples, voicegroups and a soundfont
units.detail: Asset extraction (docs/decisions.md, decision 2, 'Two views of a ROM', june 2026-10-26): graphics and music out of a ROM with no hand reading of its code, by watching where the game's data goes at run time. Emerald first; pret's pokeemerald is the oracle. Design: docs/asset-extraction-design.md. The design's Samples and voicegroups section: direct-sound WaveData to WAV (own RIFF writer with smpl, agbp, agbl chunks; DPCM cries decoded), programmable waves to .pcm, voicegroups to TOML, and an SF2 soundfont so the MIDI plays with Emerald's instruments. check-pret: our .wav through wav2agb against pret's direct_sound_samples .bin and the ROM's bytes; .pcm equal pret's. Report samples exact, of 544.

record.evidence: just assets-check-samples: 544 of 544 samples (388 DPCM cries) through pret's wav2agb equal pret's .bin and the ROM's bytes; 21 of 25 programmable .pcm equal pret's (4 unused by any voice). 193 voicegroup TOMLs, 176 per-voicegroup SF2s (structure tested). just check passes after merging main.

notes.text: SF2s are checked for structure only; nobody has listened to one yet (no fluidsynth on quack). Rerunning just assets-songs rewrites manifest.toml, so run just assets-samples after it. The 4 unused programmable waves aren't exported.

crates/assets exists (gbaa-assets). out/assets/emerald/manifest.toml [songs] gives each song's voicegroup address; m4a::Mem/Header/decode_song read the ROM. Add [samples]/[voicegroups] to that manifest; check-pret lives in assets::pret.

units.title: Spike: does fuzzing reveal graphics and code routes miss?
units.detail: june wants a CPU-heavy answer tried before a token-heavy one. Drive Emerald headless under the interpreter with random/mutated inputs from mutated saves and RAM/game state (party, bag, flags, map, menus), many cheap runs, no agent in the loop. Coverage feedback: keep inputs/states that load new blobs (the load log) or reach new code. Report: graphics found vs routes' ~100 and pret's ~7,600, new code addresses vs discovery, CPU-hours spent, how the curve flattens. Then the overseer brings {q:asset-extraction-reach-graphics-route} back to june with these results.

record.evidence: just fuzz-coverage (crates/fuzz), 10 workers x 45 min on quack = 7.5 CPU-hours, 4.0M frames, 0 faults: graphics (blobs+copied ranges reaching screen) 2,334 vs route's 95; source-map image/palette symbols 1,203 vs route 94 (pret ~7,608 INCGFX, so ~16%); 47 new screens (bag, party, summary, Pokédex, battle, trainer card); ROM instructions 210,748 vs 40,170; pret functions 4,903 vs 1,153, 84 of them not among discovery's starts. Curve: ~400 image symbols the first CPU-hour, then ~110/CPU-hour, not flat; screens flat by ~3 CPU-hours. docs/research/fuzz-coverage.md; just check passes after merging main.

notes.text: For the graphics-coverage question: fuzzing is option d. Next cheap steps (not built): share the corpus across workers, seed saves at story points, species/item sweeps, pair with the static LZ77 scan. Rerun: just fuzz-coverage NAME WORKERS MINUTES.

units.title: Coverage report: Emerald graphics found vs pret's used ones
units.detail: The denominator for june's ~90% target (june 2026-10-29). List pret's Emerald image and palette files, map each to ROM symbols/ranges via the source map, mark the ones never used in play (unreferenced, debug, cut content) with the reason, and score a fuzz or route output against the rest: found with palette, found greyscale, missing, by kind (Pokémon pics, icons, tilesets, trainers, UI...). Rust, a just recipe; rescore the spike's run. Design: docs/asset-extraction-design.md, 'Graphics coverage'.

record.evidence: just assets-coverage (gbaa-assets coverage, crates/assets/src/coverage.rs): pret's 7,586 INCGFX files joined to the ROM by the source map; 181 left out as never used in play (135 named unused, 35 unreferenced, 10 placeholder Pokémon pics, 1 built out), 7,405 used. Spike's fuzz run rescored: 1,609 found (21.7%): images 802/3,875 (576 with palette, 132 greyscale, 94 unpaired), palettes 734/3,236, tilemaps 73/294, by kind in out/fuzz/spike/coverage.txt; route phase 132 (1.8%), route manifest 107. New unit test passes; just check passes after merging main.

notes.text: Palette pairing is a heuristic (same folder or file name in pret); unreferenced = no aligned ROM word into the symbol. Fuzz palettes are found by load rows, since fade code drops provenance tags before palette RAM. Rerun: just assets-coverage RUN.
